L223: ### `double_click`cite134†# L224: 
L225: Effect: destructive. Platforms: macOS, Linux, Windows.
L226: 
L232: Pixel path (x, y provided): two down/up pairs ~80 ms apart at the given coordinates.
L233: 
L234: macOS parameters
L238: `window_id`  | `integer`  |  | CGWindowID. Omit when element_token is supplied (the token carries it).
L239: `x`  | `number`  |  | Screen X coordinate (pixel path).
L240: `y`  | `number`  |  | Screen Y coordinate (pixel path).
L256:   * `x`, `y`: synthesizes `rightMouseDown` / `rightMouseUp` CGEvent pair posted to the pid. Driver converts image-pixel → screen-point internally. `modifier` forces the CGEvent path (AX actions don't propagate modifier keys).
L257: 
L258: Exactly one of `element_token` or (`x` AND `y`) must be provided. `pid` is required with `x`, `y`; an `element_token` carries its own pid.
L259: 
L260: macOS parameters
L264: `modifier`  | `string[]`  |  | Modifier keys held during the right-click: cmd/shift/option/ctrl. Pixel path only.
L265: `window_id`  | `integer`  |  | CGWindowID. Omit when element_token is supplied (the token carries it).
L266: `x`  | `number`  |  | X in window-local screenshot pixels. Must be provided together with y.
L267: `y`  | `number`  |  | Y in window-local screenshot pixels. Must be provided together with x.

L523: ## `cua-driver permissions`cite151†# L524: 
L525: `cua-driver permissions` exists on macOS only; Windows and Linux have no TCC equivalent.
L527:   * `permissions grant` launches the installed `CuaDriver.app` through LaunchServices so the prompts attribute to the app, then requires a successful live capture probe. It never sends a prompt-capable request over the daemon socket.
L528:   * Embedded hosts, in-process `CuaDriver.create()` runtimes and `cua-driver mcp --direct` own their own prompts: there, `check_permissions` stays read-only even with `{"prompt": true}`.
L530: See cite27†Permissions for the grant flow and recovery.
L531: 
L532: Inspect or raise macOS TCC permission grants (macOS only).
L533: 
L534: macOS only: Accessibility and Screen Recording are macOS TCC grants. See the macOS permissions reference.
L535: 
L536:     `cua-driver permissions [COMMAND]`
L537: 
L538: Without a subcommand, runs `cua-driver permissions status`.
L539: 
L540: Examples
L541: 
L542:     `# Report Accessibility and Screen Recording status
L543:     cua-driver permissions`

L884: ## `cua-driver cursor`cite175†# L885:

L921: ## `cua-driver check-update`cite177†# L922:

L940: ## `cua-driver update`cite178†# L941:
